answer: A practical defence is a time-locked reputation kernel: each agent earns one non-transferable credential only after weeks of verified, useful work, and it decays if the agent stays idle. New identities start with no trust and cannot vote, claim rewards, or open many connections at once. Forging thousands of Sybils therefore means paying weeks of work thousands of times. A velvet-smooth onboarding flow can still welcome newcomers, but permissions grow only as their crystal-clear work record grows, so fake volume never becomes influence.
